newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's 18-mo bills yields to debut at 5.31/32%.
newsitem.headline: Spain's 18-mo bills yields to debut at 5.31/32%.

text.p: Yields of Spanish 18-month bills are set to debut on Monday at around 5.31/32 percent with heavy demand, dealers said on Friday.
They added yields of one-year bills are expected either to remain steady or fall a bit from 5.363 percent set on April 16, only one day after the last rate cut by the Bank of Spain.
On Friday afternoon grey-market bills were yielding around 5.28/30 percent for one year and at around 5.31/32 percent for 18 months.

"If the Treasury have to pay something more it will prefer to pay the higher yield for 18-month bills. It's the first time they are offering this maturity and they are interested in placing this kind of maturity," a Madrid-based dealer said.
Dealers expect the Treasury to place around 250 and 350 billion pesetas of one-year bills and around 200/250 billion pesetas of 18-month bills.
At the end of April Treasury bills for 338 billion pesetas mature.
